sanskrit: अहिंसा समता तुष्टिस्तपो दानं यशोऽयशः । भवन्ति भावा भूतानां मत्त एव पृथग्विधाः ॥
hindiTranslation: बुद्धि, ज्ञान, असम्मोह, क्षमा, सत्य, दम, शम, सुख, दुःख, भव, अभाव, भय, अभय, अहिंसा, समता, तुष्टि, तप, दान, यश और अपयश  प्राणियोंके ये अनेक प्रकारके और अलगअलग बीस भाव मेरेसे ही होते हैं ॥
englishTranslation: Nonviolence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, honor, and dishonor—all these different states of beings arise from Me alone.
essence: All qualities are expressions of the same divine source.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Nonviolence, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, honor, and dishonor all arise from Krishna alone in different beings.
simpleInsight: You do not have to manufacture your best qualities alone; they are already rooted in something larger.
detailedMeaning: Krishna says that even the finest human qualities, such as nonviolence, balance, contentment, discipline, generosity, honor, and dishonor, depend on a source. They all flow from Krishna's presence in beings.
modernRelevance: A shopkeeper is patient with one customer and snaps at the next, then wonders which one is the real him. Krishna says both calm and its loss come from a source larger than either mood.
translationLiteral: अहिंसा (nonviolence) / समता (equanimity) / तुष्टिः (contentment) / तपः (austerity) / दानम् (charity) / यशः (honor) / अयशः (dishonor) / भवन्ति (they become) / भावाḥ (states) / भूतानाम् (of beings) / मत् (from Me) / एव (only) / पृथग्विधाः (of different kinds)
insight: Krishna lists honour and dishonour side by side, both arising from him along with nonviolence and charity.

quoteVariants.text: Every human quality rises from the divine. Nothing stands apart.
Even your best traits come from the divine.
